A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLAM study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original classification experiments on five datasets, including fairness metrics, average and worst-class accuracies, and training-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those experiments and adds original results for iNaturalist2018, color jitter, reassessed ImageNet labels, hyperparameter sensitivity, and class-specific performance.

M1.justification: Equation (8) changes from projecting unnormalized weights and then normalizing to normalizing first and applying a specified Euclidean projection. Algorithm 1 replaces its exact argmin instruction with this update. These are reported procedural corrections within the retained CLAM framework; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V4 extends the original five-dataset coverage with class-imbalanced species classification on iNaturalist2018. It also adds color-jitter input conditions on four retained datasets and reassessed-label evaluation on the existing ImageNet images.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets and APStar comparison are retained. However, Figure 4 and Appendix K add explicit class-accuracy differences against Normal training to the existing training-dynamics analysis, whose earlier plots displayed CLAM weights and accuracies alone.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a τ sweep over 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, and 10; eight color-jitter configurations; reassessed-label evaluation; and best-10%-class accuracy for iNaturalist2018. These extend the evaluation procedures without a reported revision to the original ResNet-50 benchmark design.

E4.justification: V4 adds quantitative τ sensitivity, robustness to another augmentation technique, and reassessed-label checks. Appendix I examines worst-class identities and training-versus-test performance, while expanded figures show class-specific gains and losses against Normal. The APStar analysis is retained and moved, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V4 explicitly identifies Table 2's existing ± entries as mean ± standard deviation; v3's Table 2 did not name the dispersion measure. This is a reporting clarification, with no reported increase in runs or addition of seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain all numerical entries, but Tables 6–9 add substantial results. For example, iNaturalist2018 average/worst-class accuracies are 42.9%/12.5% for CLAM versus 42.1%/11.1% for Normal. New class-level difference plots also reveal both gains and losses relative to Normal.

T1.justification: V4 adds compactness, convexity, positive-weight constraints, and a mixed-strategy assumption supporting minimax equivalence. It revises the projection-related definitions and derivation in Appendix B and adds Lemma 1 with a proof concerning last-iteration loss conditional on weight convergence. Proposition 4.1 and the headline regret bound remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about CLAM, convergence, class equity, and limited average-accuracy costs. Updating the abstract from five to six datasets expands supporting evidence without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: V4 interprets improved testing accuracy despite perfect worst-class training accuracy as a reduced generalization gap, relates τ sensitivity to theory, and discusses the COV-versus-accuracy tradeoff on iNaturalist2018. It also makes the last-iteration argument conditional on converging weights. The original fairness–accuracy limitation remains.

D1.justification: V4 documents the new τ settings and brightness/contrast/saturation jitter configurations, but removes v3's explicit crop-bound range of 0.48–1 and its β explanation. Existing default hyperparameters, baseline settings, preprocessing instructions, and hardware/training-time disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Scott and Zhang (2020), Beyer et al. (2020), and Horn et al. (2018), with additional positioning around label noise, reassessed labels, and class-imbalanced data. The principal relationships to GGF, group fairness, and existing class-equity methods remain.

P1.justification: V4 makes targeted prose and terminology edits, changes author ordering and corresponding-author information, and adds acknowledgments. The APStar discussion moves from the main results section into Appendix D, while the main narrative structure remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: V4 adopts journal formatting, rearranges Figure 3 into a horizontal display, expands class-dynamics figures with accuracy-gap panels, consolidates retained appendix plots, and adds Tables 6–9. Many older plots contain identical image data despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: V4 broadens validation beyond v3 and adds theoretical assumptions and a conditional last-iteration argument. However, new Table 7 reports CIFAR-10 standard deviation 3.86% with range 24.3%, incompatible with Appendix H's definitions: that range requires at least about 5.73% standard deviation across ten classes. The revised theory also describes Euclidean projection while Appendix B uses clipping and renormalization. These unresolved empirical and theoretical inconsistencies prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
